title: Solve it: the highest bid
idea: GUIDED INTEGRATED PROBLEM. Track-the-best (max) pattern built by hand with a loop — no max() builtin.
problem: Auction bids are [120, 95, 150, 110]. Show the highest bid.

exercises.prompt:
PROBLEM: bids [120, 95, 150, 110]. Show the HIGHEST bid.

Understand — the output is...?
exercises.explanation: The output is a single value: the largest bid in the list.

exercises.prompt: This course lets us call max() to get the biggest value.
exercises.explanation: No — we build 'track the best' ourselves with a loop. Learning the pattern is the whole point; max() is never used.

exercises.prompt: Example — by hand, walk the bids keeping the best so far: 120, then 95, then 150, then 110. Final best?
exercises.explanation: Best starts at 120, 95 is smaller, 150 is bigger so best=150, 110 is smaller. Highest = 150, your check value.

exercises.prompt: By hand, why start 'best' at the FIRST bid (120) and not at 0?
exercises.explanation: Starting at the first real value is safe. Starting at 0 would be wrong if all bids were negative — a subtle edge bug.
options: The first real bid is a safe starting best; 0 could be wrong for all-negative data

exercises.prompt: Plan — track the best. Order the steps.
exercises.explanation: Set best to the first bid, then for each bid, if it beats best, replace best. Show best at the end.
blocks: Set best to the first bid
For each bid in the list
If this bid is greater than best, update best

exercises.prompt: Inside the loop, which comparison decides we found a new best?
exercises.explanation: A new best happens when the current bid is greater than the best so far — bid > best.
Seed best with the first item, scan the rest, update on a bigger value, then print. This is max built by hand.
Use > so a strictly larger bid replaces the best. We track the maximum ourselves — no max() call.

exercises.prompt: Check — it prints 150, hand example was 150. Verdict?
exercises.explanation: Output matches the hand example, so the track-the-best logic is correct.

exercises.prompt: Re-check with NEW bids [40, 40, 40]. What prints?
exercises.explanation: All equal, so best stays 40 the whole way. 'Greater than' never triggers an update, which is correct — 40 is the highest.
